gaps.sentence: The night bus runs ___ twenty minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Every twenty minutes' expresses regular intervals; 'each twenty minutes' is not used.

gaps.sentence: ___ John and his brother are doctors.
gaps.explanation: 'Both John and his brother are ...' links two people affirmatively; 'neither' and 'either' pair with 'nor/or'.

gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.

gaps.sentence: ___ attempts were made to contact her.
gaps.explanation: 'Several' is used with countable plurals; 'much', 'little' and 'a great deal of' need uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: ___ money was spent on advertising last year.
